- Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are a type of machine learning model that learn to generate new images based on existing images. 
- The model is composed of two main parts: the generator and the discriminator. The generator produces new images while the discriminator determines whether a given image is real or fake. 
- The performance of a GAN is measured by the quality of the generated images. The generator is trained to produce high-quality images while the discriminator is trained to recognize and distinguish between real and fake images. 
- The architecture of a GAN is complex and involves a large number of parameters. The generator is trained to learn from the data and improve its performance while the discriminator is trained to improve its performance. 
- Generative Adversarial Networks are used in image generation tasks such as image generation from random starting points. They are also used in other fields such as generative art and image synthesis.
